scenario_description:
Objective: Prevent a developing refrigerator-cooling problem from leaving scheduled perishables without safe storage over the weekend.
Emerging Need: An initial warm reading is explainable by an open door, but later closed-door readings show a persistent cooling fault while service capacity still exists.
Decision Context: Stored maintenance guidance determines the temperature pattern that justifies escalation, the landlord-approval route, appliance-movement limits, and the weekday cutoff.
Consequence: Once the diagnostic route closes, no spoilage is documented yet, but the delivery and current contents may face unsafe storage until Monday.

parameter.content: I had the kitchen fridge door open while wiping the shelf bins. The thermometer showed 43°F right after I closed it, but the door had been open about ten minutes. Only condiments, cans, and seltzer are in there right now.

parameter.title: Portland Pantry refrigerated grocery delivery
parameter.description: Confirmed delivery window for chilled ingredients and weekend perishables.

parameter.subject: Thursday north-route refrigerator diagnostic capacity
parameter.body: Evergreen's north-route board still has one refrigerator diagnostic hold available this afternoon. Landlord-authorized tickets can be attached while the route remains open; closed-route tickets roll to the next regular cooling visit.

parameter.content: Follow-up on the fridge: the door stayed shut after 11:30. I checked at 12:25 and it was 45.8°F, then again at 13:15 and it is 47.1°F. The freezer display says 20°F. No leaks or spoiled smells, and I cleared the cereal boxes away from the vent.

parameter.subject: North-route refrigerator diagnostics closed for today
parameter.body: Today's north-route refrigerator diagnostic board is now closed. The next regular non-emergency cooling visit available for landlord-authorized tickets is Monday morning.
